answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and therefore it pays the lagoon fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the falcon ledger attributes every share, the marble audit reveals the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 67% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 24 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
